pos.personaBrief: Argentina averaged 58.6% possession in qualifying and built through midfield, but dropped into low blocks when leading (Croatia, France, Brazil) and countered; possession was a means, not a creed.

pro.personaBrief: Short build-up with keeper short passes and a diamond around pressers, Paredes line-breaking passes, yet vertical immediate counters after regains.

est.personaBrief: Fluid system with no set shape, constant approximation and numerical superiority around the ball, Messi roaming and wide midfielders moving inside.

lar.personaBrief: Very narrow structure with central midfielders and Messi between lines, but full-backs and wing-backs gave width and Di Maria stayed wide in the final.

blo.personaBrief: Aggressive press, counter-press within seconds and matching numbers high, though a much deeper block when protecting leads.

mar.personaBrief: Man-oriented defending, one-on-ones like Bielsa, but mixed with zonal handoffs and staggered zonal corners.

pla.personaBrief: Scaloni changed systems per opponent (3-5-2, back five, 4-3-3) and said they are not one-dimensional, adapting to players such as Messi.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic, result-first: closed games with a back five when ahead, tactical fouls, tournament won on penalties.

sis.personaBrief: A well-run collective enhancing Messi, who was given freedom and no defensive duties, with others working for him.

jog.personaBrief: Technical midfield and Messi at the centre, with an aggressive press requiring intensity.

bas.personaBrief: Rejuvenated an aging squad, introducing Enzo, Alvarez, Mac Allister, mixed with veterans Messi, Otamendi, Di Maria.

lid.personaBrief: Togetherness without egos, players enjoying playing for the shirt, consultation with Messi, who was treated specially.
